title: The Uniform of the Palatinate
premise: In 1793, in the contested Palatinate borderlands, Noor Eastwick, an apprentice clockmaker of mixed heritage, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock just as occupying forces requisition the town and its census ledger. The ledger lists every resident's name and origin, and Noor's own entry — altered years ago by the late clockmaker to protect them — is the only thing keeping them invisible. When Noor discovers that Elias Voss, the young officer overseeing the requisition, is the same boy they once promised to teach watchmaking, the promise collides with the army's lists, a resistance cell hiding in the observatory's cellars, and an armistice that keeps almost being signed. Noor ultimately trades their own protected name for the town's endangered ones, forging the master clock to strike the hour of the armistice early and forcing both armies to stand down, then leaves the Palatinate carrying only their tools and a new name of their own making.
about_author: Beatrix Ashgrove is a former conservator of scientific instruments who spent a decade restoring tower clocks in small European towns before turning to fiction. She writes about people whose lives are measured in small, precise acts of courage.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Noor Eastwick, POV: arrives in the hill town of Merenzoll to repair the observatory's master clock, measuring the world in what fits in a satchel. They are quiet, precise, and determined to remain unnoticed. Emotional beat: the comfort of being useful but unseen.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Everyone
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: the town clerk Herr Brandt shows Noor the census ledger required by the new imperial decree, and Noor glimpses their own altered entry — the dead master clockmaker's quiet forgery. Emotional beat: gratitude shadowed by the fear of being found out.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: soldiers arrive to requisition the town; the ledger is seized and the observatory claimed as a signal station. Noor is ordered to keep the clock running for the garrison. Emotional beat: the world Noor carefully carried begins to be taken apart.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Knew Their Hands
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: Lieutenant Elias Voss inspects the clockwork and recognizes Noor's technique — and Noor recognizes the boy from the border fairs who once begged to be taught. Neither says it aloud. Emotional beat: a peacetime promise resurfacing like a scar.

chapters.title: Names Are Ammunition
chapters.summary: Elias, POV: Elias reviews the ledger, aware that misfiled names mean deportations, and notices one entry that has been tampered with. He says nothing. Emotional beat: the first crack in his soldier's obedience.

chapters.title: What the Cellars Keep
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: Noor discovers the resistance cell — led by the widow Marta Kellner — hiding fugitive families beneath the observatory, using the clock's chimes as their signal code. Emotional beat: invisibility revealed as a shared, fragile craft.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: a flashback to the border fair years ago — young Elias, the son of an enemy customs officer, and the promise: one lesson in watchmaking, someday. Noor realizes the debt is now due in wartime. Emotional beat: tenderness complicated by danger.

chapters.title: The Hour That Lies
chapters.summary: Noor and Marta, alternating POV: they begin using the clock to send false signals, buying the hidden families time. Elias grows suspicious of the chimes' new pattern. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of small sabotage.

chapters.title: Requisition of Souls
chapters.summary: Elias, POV: orders arrive to compile a deportation list from the ledger; Elias must certify it or be replaced by a harder man, Captain Reiner. Emotional beat: complicity closing in like a vise.

chapters.title: The Lesson, Owed
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: Elias comes at night, ostensibly to inspect the escapement, and asks for the lesson he was promised. Noor teaches him, and in the teaching they speak plainly for the first time. Emotional beat: two people briefly outside the war.

chapters.title: Reiner's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Captain Reiner, POV: Reiner suspects the observatory, cross-checks the ledger against parish records, and finds the altered entry. He sets a trap rather than an arrest. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Marta, POV: the cellar is raided; Marta is taken and the hidden families scatter into the winter hills. Noor escapes through the clock tower's weights shaft. Emotional beat: grief and survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: What Noor Carries
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: hiding in the tower, Noor takes stock — tools, the forged ledger page, Marta's signal key — and decides that running would mean the names in the ledger are lost forever. Emotional beat: the shift from hiding to choosing.

chapters.title: The Armistice That Isn't
chapters.summary: Elias, POV: an armistice is drafted and delayed three times; each delay means the deportation list executes. Elias realizes the paperwork is the weapon. Emotional beat: disillusion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias, alternating POV: they meet in the clock room and form a desperate plan — Noor will alter the master clock to strike the armistice hour early, forcing both sides to stand down while the ledger 'burns' in a staged fire. Emotional beat: trust built from mutual risk.

chapters.title: Learning the Escapement
chapters.summary: Elias, POV: Elias learns the clock's mechanism by lamplight so he can cover for Noor, understanding at last what the promise meant. Emotional beat: the lesson completed, the debt transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: The Fire That Forgives
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: the staged ledger fire goes wrong — Reiner is not fooled, and Noor is caught mid-forgery, their true name read aloud for the first time in years. Emotional beat: exposure as both catastrophe and strange relief.

chapters.title: The Hour Before
chapters.summary: Noor, imprisoned in the tower, POV: Reiner offers Noor freedom in exchange for the resistance's names; Noor instead finishes the clock's alteration through the cell bars with a file and a borrowed hand. Emotional beat: defiance measured in minutes.

chapters.title: When the Clock Spoke
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging: the master clock strikes the armistice hour early; bells answer across the valley; soldiers on both sides stand down in confusion, and Elias stalls Reiner's execution order in the resulting paralysis. Emotional beat: the climax — a town holding its breath inside a lie told for mercy.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Escapement
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias, POV: Reiner's counter-order comes, but the armistice is signed hours later, making Noor's false hour prophecy rather than treason; Elias testifies that the clock, not a person, struck it. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, outside the law.

chapters.title: Names Returned
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: Marta is freed, the hidden families return, and the ledger is rewritten openly — every name restored, including Noor's, written this time in Noor's own hand. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than forged.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Noor, POV: with the war's paperwork settled and the clock running true, Noor packs their satchel, keeps one gear from the master clock, and walks out of Merenzoll at dawn as Elias watches from the tower. Emotional beat: departure not as exile but as a self-authored beginning.
